0.changes: Nothing worth changing: your notes already found two working methods (broil then 300°F finish, or marinate 30 min and grill), solving the broiler-strength issue readers report.

1.changes: Shock the eggs in ice water immediately after the 10-minute rest instead of cooling in the pan; this is the most-repeated reader fix for peeling and costs nothing since your timing already works.

2.changes: Hold back about 50 g of the 459 g water at mixing — multiple bakers found this dough too slack to build strength, especially in humid weather. If centers stay underdone, drop to 425°F and add 5-10 minutes.

3.changes: Bump the oven to 320-325°F; readers report undercooked beef/potatoes even at the updated 300°F, matching your 3/23 'wiggly bits' note. Skip the final stovetop reduction — your own note found it usually unnecessary.

4.changes: Brush the beef with soy sauce and let it sit a few minutes before applying the rub; the top-voted reader fix (300+ combined votes) for a better crust. Adds about 5 minutes, no extra gear.

6.changes: Boil both citrus whole, then for the lemon scoop out and discard the inside pulp, keeping only the rind; for the orange keep everything but the seeds. This is the recipe's own ambiguous instruction, per the comment consensus.

14.changes: Nothing worth changing. The family has used this exact method reliably since 2020, cucumber draining (the one step that matters) is already in the recipe, and reader comments confirm no real complaints.

17.changes: Tent the rolls with foil for the first 10 minutes of baking, then uncover to finish; the most-repeated reader fix for burnt tops and soggy bottoms, and costs no extra time.

24.changes: Add a second 5-minute rest partway through rolling, on top of the initial hour rest; this relaxes the gluten for smoother sheets and is the top reader tip (155 votes). Adds about 5 minutes.

32.changes: Swap the whole almonds for sliced almonds; the logs are fragile to slice as the recipe itself warns, and sliced almonds make clean cuts much easier. No added time, same toasting step.

34.changes: Add 6-8 whole peppercorns to the pot before simmering, then strain them out with the seeds — the sauce's most-repeated reader amendment. Since you already strain for seeds, this costs no extra time.

44.changes: Dice the chard stalks and add them with the onion and fennel to cook longer before the leaves go in, instead of discarding — likely why your 11/24 note found the chard tough.

46.changes: Nothing worth changing. The family already prefers this over Bon Appétit's version for its thickness, and readers' suggestions (carrot, potato, bacon) are additions, not fixes to a real problem.

49.changes: Nothing worth changing. This is the family's long-standing standby, and the source page is too thin (2 comments, 17 ratings) to support a confident swap to grilling over broiling.

56.changes: Cut the woody ends evenly about 1/2 inch rather than snapping at the natural break point — wastes noticeably less asparagus for the same result; peeling thick stalks as written is correct.

57.changes: Double the blue cheese to 4 oz, as your 8/18 note already found necessary. Mix a few hours or overnight ahead — readers report the flavor is muted when served immediately.

58.changes: Roast on a bed of sliced potatoes in the Lodge cast iron skillet instead of a foil-lined rack — catches the buttermilk drippings and resolves readers' most-voted complaint. Adds about 10 minutes for slicing.

59.changes: If waffles turn out flat, thin store-bought buttermilk is the likely cause; swap in thick buttermilk or plain kefir, which readers found gives crisper, better-risen waffles for no extra time.

60.changes: Cut the pepper to a scant 1/2 teaspoon and salt the pasta water lightly — your 11/21 note found both overdone. The Microplane-fine grated cheese called for is already correct; keep that.

63.changes: Caramelize onion and fennel at medium, not medium-high — readers report the stated heat scorches it in most pots. Cut rosemary to 1 tablespoon; as written it overwhelms the faint fennel flavor.

67.changes: Bake 20 minutes covered, then 40 uncovered — your 2/19 note found this fixes the wateriness, proven across four batches. The recipe as written (10-15 covered, 35-40 uncovered) undercooks the covered stage.

69.changes: Cook the farro to tenderness by tasting rather than the stated 30 minutes — pearled vs. whole farro vary widely in cook time. Cut the cooking-liquid salt somewhat; the Parmesan on top adds plenty.

71.changes: Nothing worth changing. The salt and asparagus quantities are already what the single detailed review confirms works, and review volume is too thin for further correction.

81.changes: Swap the 2 cups water for chicken broth or a splash of white wine; readers overwhelmingly report the water-based sauce tastes bland and flat.

82.changes: Boil the spaghetti in chicken broth instead of water and use that broth for the sauce; the top-voted fix (132 votes) says it transforms the dish.

83.changes: Skip broiling fresh tomatoes and use one 28-oz can fire-roasted tomatoes instead, per the two highest-voted notes (177, 122); keep charring the onion, garlic and jalapeños for flavor.

84.changes: Finish the last 20-25 minutes on convection (you have two convection ovens) to fully set the crust — your 1/26 note flagged uncertain doneness on a regular bake. No added time.

88.changes: Swap the pork loin for boneless pork shoulder; loin is lean and readers report the recipe's rapid pressure-cooking dries it out, while shoulder stays moist under the same treatment.

98.changes: Add about 1/3 cup ricotta to the filling, as your 4/24 note wondered — commenters independently describe the same dry, burger-like texture without a softening addition like ricotta.

99.changes: Nothing worth changing. Your 7/17 note confirms Kenji's method as written — 2 tsp salt on the tomatoes was enough, lighter sourdough beat heavy multigrain, and no reader correction to quantities exists.

100.changes: Toss the pasta with the tomato sauce first, then fold in the fried eggplant afterward rather than simmering it in the sauce — the top-voted fix (140 votes) says the eggplant flavor otherwise disappears.

106.changes: Dress the noodles with the peanut sauce first, then pile the raw vegetables on top rather than tossing everything together; the top-voted tip (687) keeps the vegetables crisp and colorful.

108.changes: Cut the salt by about 1 teaspoon if using table salt, not Diamond Crystal — your 2009/2010 notes both found it too salty. Budget closer to 3 hours in the oven, as your 2024 note found, not 2.5.

112.changes: Salt chicken before browning and increase stock to ~3 cups (or use one chicken) — your 1/22 note found sauce ran short. Pour off excess bacon fat before adding wine; article says to, recipe steps don't.

119.changes: A full pound of fresh spinach needs well over 4 minutes to wilt down, per reader consensus (197 votes) — cook until fully collapsed, not by the clock. Finish with lemon zest and juice; it cuts the cream's richness.

120.changes: Nothing worth changing. The gram weights already resolve the Diamond Crystal vs. Morton salt confusion that caused most complaints, and the purge-rinse-dry steps readers needed are already in the method.

121.changes: Nothing worth changing. The top reader tip — simmering cobs for stock — meaningfully lengthens a 30-minute dish for a modest gain; the built-in chile flakes and lemon already address the sweetness some found cloying.

122.changes: Nothing worth changing. Your 8/21 note confirms garlic powder works fine, and reviewers report no technique or timing problems — the fresh dill and quick sear are already right.

126.changes: Brussels sprouts often aren't tender in the stated 3-5 minutes — the single most-reported problem. Cover the skillet for a couple extra minutes after browning to steam them through before adding the red pepper flakes.

131.changes: Brown the chops plain first, then coat with mustard and cumin before the oven — coating them before searing scorches the mustard and is why readers say they don't brown well (top-voted fix).

133.changes: Double the sauce ingredients (broth, cream, butter) — readers agree the sauce, not the chicken, makes the dish and the given amount is too skimpy. Use more curry powder than stated; cooks report going bolder pays off.

137.changes: Your 1/22 note found it — low-fat string cheese turns hard; use real brick cheese (or 50/50 mozzarella-Jack) for the buttery drip. Bake on the middle rack at 550°F, not the lowest — bottom-rack burning is the top complaint.

140.changes: Leave the turkey uncovered on a rack in the fridge for at least the last day instead of a sealed bag — trapped moisture undercuts dry-brining's crisp-skin goal, the top reader complaint. Keep spatchcocking; your 11/24 note found it works.

142.changes: Nothing worth changing. Your 7/2021 note confirms it works well as written, and the most-helpful review (815 votes) says not to complicate a dressing that's already balanced.

144.changes: Nothing worth changing. No reader has actually cooked this, but the technique — toast the grain, deglaze with wine, add broth gradually — is standard and already correct.

147.changes: Roast beets at 400°F ~45 min or pressure-cook 15 min — the method never says how, despite assuming roasted beets. Cut olive oil to 6 tbsp (81 g); readers found 1/2 cup excessive.

150.changes: Nothing worth changing. Your 2/25 note already found the fix — keep enough liquid — and the direction already reserves pasta water for exactly that. Off-heat egg-cream mixing already prevents scrambling.

152.changes: Cook the asparagus in the pasta water the last 2 minutes instead of steaming separately; the top reader tip (408 votes), confirmed by others, saves a pan and the rinse-and-drain step.

153.changes: Squeeze sausage from its casings and crumble while browning instead of cutting chunks — better coverage and sear, the most-endorsed reader fix. Add a splash more cream; readers found the sauce too thin for a full pound of pasta.

156.changes: Nothing worth changing. Your 9/18 note already confirmed halibut works well with this method, and the pan-frying temperature and technique in the directions are already correct.

157.changes: Don't treat the cumin and chipotle powder in the slaw as optional — readers report it's bland without them. Double the corn tortillas per taco; a single one won't hold without cracking.

159.changes: Nothing worth changing. Steaming rather than boiling and seasoning at the very end are already the tested method here; the reader notes are about reheating leftovers, not the base recipe.

161.changes: Nothing worth changing. Your RM 3/13 note already dialed in the ratios — 5 oz cheese per pizza, half recipe for a 12-inch pan — and the bottom-crisping stovetop fix readers recommend is already in the directions.

162.changes: Roll the dough out on parchment paper, then slide the paper straight onto the sheet pan — the top reader tip, removes the transfer risk of a crude free-form dough at zero added cost.

163.changes: If you substitute Worcestershire for fish sauce, as your recent notes do, cap it at 1/2 teaspoon — the most-voted review warns a full teaspoon overpowers. Your own onion-quantity and salt fixes already solved the yield and blandness issues.

165.changes: Directions give both round-cake (35-40 min) and loaf (50-55 min) times but only the loaf pan is specified; bake 50-55 minutes and ignore the round timing. Trim oil to 1/3 cup per the top-voted fix.

168.changes: Your note already caught the leaking; the real fix is draining the sugared fruit 15-20 minutes (during the dough's chill) before piling, not just parchment underneath. Adds 0 minutes since it overlaps with chill time.

171.changes: Your 5/24 note already found the fix: sear at medium, not medium-high, to stop the scorching Steph disliked, and steam covered 13 minutes rather than 15 — already dialed in correctly.

173.changes: Nothing worth changing. The ganache-vs-glaze debate in the comments is taste preference, not a fix, and the almond-flour equivalence is already handled by the ingredient list as written.

177.changes: Skip the 30-60 min lemon marinade; the 52-vote fix says it's unneeded and total time is far under the stated two hours. Drop the tomato paste too — tomatoes alone keep the sauce lighter (62 votes).

179.changes: Your 5/21 note already found the burning and over-strong lemon. Drop the chicken broth per the 1,041-vote fix — its sugars likely cause the scorching — and cut lemon juice to 1/3 cup.

181.changes: Nothing worth changing. Commenters raise no issues with the vinaigrette ratios or the resting time; the discussion is only about optional swaps and mix-ins that don't apply to this version.

182.changes: Nothing worth changing. Same vinaigrette and rest time as the collection's other Ina Garten Greek salad; commenters report no problems with proportions, only optional add-ins like grilled chicken or pasta.

185.changes: Nothing worth changing. Your 5/21 note confirms it worked well with a top sirloin swap and the California rub; the written sear-then-indirect-heat method already matches the top-voted reader technique.

186.changes: The 'tarry' taste Steph noticed is likely garlic in the pre-grill brush scorching over direct heat; brush with plain oil first, add garlic only in the post-grill toss. Reviewers also report it runs salty — cut to 2 teaspoons.

187.changes: Nothing worth changing. No corrections are reported; commenters discuss only optional swaps like habanero for jalapeno or red onion for yellow, not fixes to technique, ratios, or resting time.

191.changes: Roast to 145F, not 137F as written, then tent 10 minutes -- your 6/2023 note already found this doneness and confirmed it stays tender. No change to the acidic marinade; three uses across 6 years show no complaints.

207.changes: Nothing worth changing. Readers' Morton-vs-Diamond-Crystal salt confusion is already resolved by the 5.6 g weight given in the ingredient line, and the built-in test-patty step catches any other seasoning issues before you commit the batch.

208.changes: Bake in a 10-inch pan (most home cooks lack an 11-inch) a few minutes longer. Bump lemon to zest of 2 large lemons plus 1 tbsp juice, the most successful reader tweak, well short of riskier 3-4-lemon versions.

210.changes: Nothing worth changing. Dill, not basil, is already the herb specified, matching what commenters insist is essential to this version, and baking rather than browning the meatballs already keeps the broth clear.

214.changes: Skip the sugar for the Ooni: 900F browns the crust in under 90 seconds on its own, and added sugar risks scorching before it cooks through. For cast iron, pre-cook the dough dry and oiled 1-2 min before topping.

215.changes: Nothing worth changing. The gram weight already prevents the table-salt-vs-Diamond-Crystal mistake the recipe's own note flags, and the most-voted rebuttal (630 votes) confirms it works as written despite the naming argument in the comments.

217.changes: Keep the 8-inch springform as written. Readers who scaled to a 9-inch got a thin crust and filling even after increasing yolks, juice, and condensed milk -- the pan swap, not the ratios, is the real failure point.

218.changes: Nothing worth changing. Cast iron or heavy stainless is already specified instead of a wok, batches prevent overcrowding, and the Asian-pear-vs-pineapple substitution guidance is already built in. Reader comments here are speculative riffs, not real fixes.

222.changes: Your 4/23 note already found the fix for this recipe's well-known bug: the published method never says when the potatoes go in (a 1991 NYT correction confirms it). They simmer fine straight in the broth, no separate step.

223.changes: Blanch the sugar snap peas 1 minute and slice crosswise instead of lengthwise before stirring in -- the top reader tip, keeps them green and crisp instead of tasting raw. Adds about 3 minutes.

224.changes: Your 6/25 note already flagged the problem: finish with a few extra minutes at 400F instead of the low broil, which charred the cheese last time. Same total time, no new step.

227.changes: Hold the curd at a full rolling boil for close to a full minute, not just until it thickens — the top-voted fix for the runny-curd problem readers report. If it still weeps, swap cornstarch for potato starch.

229.changes: Nothing worth changing. The one substantive reader fix — weighing flour instead of scooping — is already built into this recipe's gram weights, so the density problem commenters describe doesn't apply here.

231.changes: Rebalance toward more beans and broth and less shrimp — the reader-consensus fix (741 votes), and it may explain why your 6/2025 attempt read as 'different' and underwhelming. No added time.

232.changes: Bake and set the mousse layer in a springform pan instead of transferring it back into a standard cake pan — the top reader fix; it removes the fragile pan-swap the current method requires. No added time.

238.changes: Add salt — the recipe omits it and several readers note the salsa tastes flat without it; salt to taste after the rest. Resting longer, even overnight, further melds the flavors per top reviews. No added time.

239.changes: Cool the cake 15 minutes, not 5, before inverting — this prevents the pear layer and caramel from breaking apart on the flip. +10 min. Your note calls it delicious, so leave the sweetness alone despite online complaints.

240.changes: Nothing worth changing. This is the well-tested Essentials of Classic Italian Cooking version, and reader consensus says follow it exactly; the fat separating out at the end is expected, not a sign to skim.

246.changes: Nothing worth changing. Your 6/22 note already confirms the method — fried, disher-scooped for even size, panko and egg for binding — produced tender meatballs that held together well.

247.changes: Mix the yeast, yogurt and sugar with the milk first, then add flour gradually and hold some back — readers agree the stated flour-to-liquid ratio runs too dry and needs adjusting by feel. No added time.

248.changes: No wok: char the corn dry in the Lodge cast iron on the high burner instead — matches your 7/22 hunch that indoors works better. Budget 20 minutes for full char, not 10, and don't stir too often. +10 min.

249.changes: Skip frying the tortillas and stir in a handful of coarsely crushed tortilla chips instead — several cooks report the same crunch for one less pan and less hands-on time. Saves 5 min.

255.changes: The six-strand braid instructions are garbled per readers (560 votes); follow a standard six-strand video tutorial instead of the text. Weights are already in the ingredient list.

256.changes: Add the coleslaw mix in the last minute, not the full 10; simmering it the whole time turns it to mush per multiple reports. Your 5/25 note found the recipe good as-is on sweetness, so keep the sugar.

259.changes: Nothing worth changing. This is Kenji's tested, side-by-side-compared formula; the loudest comments are an authenticity argument about cooked vs. raw sauce, not a fixable error.

261.changes: Nothing worth changing. The family already rates this their favorite; it's the pre-1990s Quaker formula with the water that gives the crisp edge, not the reformulated all-butter version.

262.changes: Cook this on the Weber griddle outdoors instead of an indoor skillet — readers (106+58 votes) confirm it avoids filling the house with onion smoke, with zero change to the method.

265.changes: Add 2-3 minced garlic cloves and a pinch of red pepper flakes with the dry pasta at the start; the recipe omits garlic entirely, and readers' top fix (695 votes) is more aggressive seasoning.

269.changes: Nothing worth changing. Your 9/25 note already dialed in the sugar, pan size, plum count and bake time; measuring flour by weight (120 g) also sidesteps the famous sifted-flour ambiguity.

273.changes: Your 7/2019 note already found this: swap tarragon for thyme and salt lighter, plus flounder works fine in place of mercury-heavy tilefish, which several commenters flag as a species to avoid.

274.changes: Keep 60-80 g extra flour ready if the dough won't clear the bowl, a known failure point. Proof only to ~2 cm below the rim and cool loaves on their side, not hanging — hanging splits the tops.

276.changes: Your 12/25 note already worked around this formula's notoriously slack dough by using Massari's dough recipe — keep doing that. The glaze's 'corn flour' means cornstarch (UK term), not corn flour; use cornstarch, no special sourcing needed.

277.changes: Skip blanching the greens separately: chop raw and stir into the pasta water for the last minute, then drain together, per the top-voted fix — one less pan and step for the same result.

280.changes: Add 2 minced garlic cloves to the breadcrumb crust; your 4/25 note suggested this independently, and it's the most-praised fix in reviews (30+ votes). Your thermometer-based timing is already correct — no change needed there.

282.changes: Add the wine with the beef, not stirred in near the end — the top-voted fix (287 votes). Skip par-boiling the onions; slice raw and sweat them with the beef instead, saving about 15 minutes.

283.changes: Your 4/1/21 note found this: with fresh pasta, cut guanciale to about 2/3 (150 g) and add pasta water more gradually — fresh pasta's lower starch is why the sauce didn't emulsify, not the technique.

284.changes: Use 4 tablespoons butter (57 g), the low end — top correction (129 votes) says more overwhelms the cheese. Stage pine nuts, lemon and bacon before draining pasta, or it turns sticky waiting.

292.changes: Macerate the sliced peaches in the sugar 30 minutes while the dough chills, drain, and thicken the reserved juice with cornstarch before filling — fixes the recipe's top complaint, a runny pie. Bake on the lowest rack.

293.changes: Pour 1/2 cup broth or wine into the pan before roasting; the vegetables otherwise scorch before the chicken finishes at 425°F. Swap potatoes for fennel if anise isn't wanted — loses nothing per reviewers.

294.changes: Your 10/2020 note already found this: add the apples partway through their sauté (or use firmer Honeycrisp/Fuji) so they don't turn to mush by the time the pork finishes roasting. No time change.

297.changes: Wilt the chopped chard in the same skillet right after the onions, skipping the separate blanching pot and ice bath — cuts a pan, per commenters (14 votes). Pizza browns fast at 500°F; check at 6 minutes, not 10.

302.changes: Your 11/30 note already diagnosed the problem: it hit 165°F instead of the 135°F target. Pull at 128-130°F — carryover brings it to 135-140 — and probe away from the stuffed pocket, which reads hot early.

303.changes: Braise the pork a day ahead: tear it while still warm and refrigerate in the strained broth overnight — the top-voted fix (42 votes), and it noticeably improves flavor. Otherwise nothing to change; the reduction already builds the sauce.

307.changes: Nothing to fix in the method. Per your 7/12 note, use closer to the full 1 cup mayo rather than the half-cup you tried, which that note found under-dressed; keep the red-wine-vinegar swap for buttermilk.

310.changes: Nothing worth changing here. You've already fixed it — doubled spinach, added dill, subbed bouillon and creme fraiche for depth. The recipe's ratios and timing are sound as printed.

313.changes: Your 6/24 note found it: dried chickpeas undercooked, skins took 30 min to peel. Add 1/2 tsp baking soda to the soak and cook water — it softens beans faster and loosens skins so peeling is nearly unnecessary.

314.changes: Skip the 4-hour soak: boil the beans 20 minutes, then let sit off heat about an hour, per the top-voted New Orleans note — same result, hours less waiting. Finish with a splash of vinegar for brightness.

315.changes: Your own note already fixed the too-much-liquid complaint (2,196 votes) by cutting to 1 cup water. Add extra lemon juice at the end — near-universal reader fix, costs nothing.

320.changes: Double the vinegar-chile dressing and stir some into the pork rather than using it only as a garnish drizzle — the top reader fix (191 votes) for pork that tastes plain on its own.

321.changes: Nothing worth changing. No cooks note flags a problem, and reader comments are only about substitutions (plant sausage, broth for wine) that don't touch the base technique.

322.changes: Add a pinch of grated nutmeg with the cream — missing from the ingredient list but called non-negotiable by readers (352 votes). Use your widest pot for the wine/broth reduction; it cuts that simmer time noticeably.

323.changes: Your 8/22 note flagged spatter and asked about a taller pot — skip that; finish uncovered in a 400°F oven instead of reducing on the stovetop, the top reader fix (1,384 votes), and it crisps the skin too.

324.changes: Peel the shrimp and simmer the shells into the stock before cooking the rice — fixes the near-unanimous shell complaint and the flavor you found lacking in your 2/23 note. Stir lemon juice into the rice itself, not just zest.

329.changes: Nothing worth changing. The method is already the one commenters treat as a benchmark; the only complaints are enrichments (bacon fat, garlic, parmesan) that are optional, not fixes.

330.changes: Fix the gram error: 1 pint is 'about a pound' (454 g), not the listed 176 g — trusting the gram figure would badly under-fill the pan. Sear a fixed 3-4 min rather than trusting the unverifiable 'undisturbed' cue.

333.changes: The 208-vote consensus says the dish is too oily; cut the dressing oil from 1/4 cup to 2-3 tablespoons. Use mild Castelvetrano olives rather than saltier ones, per the well-liked reader tip.

335.changes: Skip the flour dredge - the top-voted fix (327 votes) says it barely sticks and adds little; use cornstarch instead for a crisper coat with no other change to the method.

336.changes: Skip oiling the foil, per the 3,190-vote top fix, so the salmon skin sticks to the foil and the flesh lifts away clean. Keep roasting rather than switching to broiling; a strongly voted rebuttal says broiling dries the fish.

346.changes: Your 10/2020 note already found the fix: skip the pepper-boil-then-grill sequence and bake at 400 for 15 minutes, then broil 4 minutes. Simpler, no grill needed, nothing else to change.

347.changes: Pat scallops dry and refrigerate uncovered up to 30 minutes before searing for a firmer, better-browning surface, per the top reader tip; pull the tough side muscle first. Buy dry-packed, not wet-packed, scallops - wet ones will not sear.

348.changes: Nothing worth changing beyond what your 4/23 note already applies - slicing the potatoes into salted water and using the mandoline's thick setting. Reviewers' only caution, that cleaning leeks is fiddly, is already assumed.

349.changes: The 32-review consensus says pull the eggs earlier than 12 minutes; the full boil leaves rubbery whites and a grey ring, so try 9-10 minutes. Mist the coated eggs with oil before baking so they brown.

352.changes: The top-voted fix (2,039 votes, independently confirmed) says the oven overcooks the eggs, setting whites while yolks go hard. Simmer covered on the stovetop instead and skip the oven; crush the tomatoes further to avoid a watery sauce.

354.changes: Nothing worth changing. Your 2/22/25 note already confirms the recipe as written - garlicky, orzo starch thickened the sauce nicely with the full 2 cups of liquid - so skip the reader tweaks to cut it back.

358.changes: On your actual gas cooktop and Lodge cast iron, don't chase 'nearly smoking' heat - the top comments warn a screaming pan burns the fond before the sauce reduces and can trip smoke alarms; use high, not max, heat.

360.changes: Ignore the 2-3 hour estimate; the dominant reviewer correction says a 3-4 lb roast hits 120-125F in 60-100 minutes at 225F, so start probing around 45 minutes. Insert the probe straight, not angled, for an accurate reading.

362.changes: Nothing worth changing. Cooking to temperature already accounts for frozen berries' extra water; your 5/22 note shows the halved, frozen-berry version worked fine as a galette filling. No reported set or ratio problems.

367.changes: Confirm the starter is active with the float test (spoonful should float) before mixing — top source of dense loaves (165 votes). Line the towel with parchment; lift dough into the hot pot by the paper, not inverting (764 votes).

368.changes: Nothing worth changing. The recipe already prints grams for its own ingredients; the top comments are a generic cups-vs-grams debate, not a fault with these amounts. Buttermilk/yogurt and flour swaps are optional, not fixes.

370.changes: Your 5/26-10/22 notes already established ~50% yield; buy 7-8+ lb shoulder, not 5.3 lb. Skip the 90-min oven bark step entirely — commenters report it dries out meat already tender from the bath; sear portions in the Lodge instead.

371.changes: Below 140F, skip raw garlic in the bag — a sealed anaerobic pouch at that temperature is a real C. botulinum risk per reader safety warnings, not just flavor advice. Add garlic to the pan sear instead.

373.changes: Nothing worth changing. The recipe's own chipotle-in-adobo already supplies the heat; your 8/25 note found adding extra Wegmans adobo marinade fails — use Sriracha instead if more heat is wanted, as you noted.

377.changes: Add a squeeze of lime or lemon juice at serving — the recipe omits acid and many cooks call it flat without it; costs nothing. Your 11/2020 note already fixed the over-spicing, halving flakes to 1/2 tsp, confirmed good 1/26.

379.changes: If freezing logs longer than about a week, expect a harmless greenish oil to weep out on thawing — bake anyway, only appearance is affected, taste and texture are unchanged. No prep change needed.

380.changes: Cut the bechamel milk to 4 cups (976 g) instead of 5 — a cook who made this two Christmases running found 5 cups too loose; easy to thin further later if needed.

384.changes: Nothing structural to fix — real meringue (your 7/24 note) is what commenters insist keeps this an Eton mess, not a trifle. Try 2 Tbsp lime juice instead of 1; a reader's accidental double dose improved it.

386.changes: Nothing worth changing. The family card already carries the technique Betty Crocker's own page omits — sugar the berries, blend wet into the fruit, mix dry in only until just moist — and no note or comment flags a problem.

389.changes: Whisk the ricotta, red pepper flakes and lemon zest with the pasta water in a bowl before adding to the pan (1,349-vote fix) — prevents the ricotta seizing into curds. Cook garlic with the onions, not separately.

390.changes: Nothing worth changing. Shrimp already gets seared first and returned only at the end, which is the fix others need; your 7/21 note confirms the dish already works well as written.

391.changes: Nothing worth changing. Quantities aren't disputed and the recipe already ranges the oil (3/4 to 1 cup) to match oil-packed vs. dry-packed tomatoes, which is the only real variable.

397.changes: If Chinese sesame paste isn't on hand, sub tahini plus a little extra toasted sesame oil (already using peanut butter for emulsion) — the recipe already specifies fresh/frozen noodles, avoiding the top reader mistake of using dried.

399.changes: Skip most of the hourly stretch-and-folds; a 166-vote baker reports loaves turn out the same without the full 3-hour fold routine. Keep the fold right after mixing in salt for structure.

400.changes: Pull waffles at medium brown, not dark — several readers report darker waffles dry out and toughen. Your notes already solved the butter-clumping and yield issues; this doneness cue is the one gap.

401.changes: Nothing worth changing. Frying the paste before adding liquid is already the method here, and the 4-6 tbsp range already lets you dial heat down if the full amount runs too spicy.

402.changes: Your 8/24 note already found the heat problem — keep pepper flakes at 1/2 tsp. Several cooks report the reduction finishing in 3-4 hours, not 5-6; start checking early to avoid scorching or paste-stage.

403.changes: Bake time depends on cutter size: the written 6-8 minutes only suits ~2-inch cutters — large cutters need 12-13 minutes, thin ones 8-9. Also spoon-and-level the flour rather than packing to avoid tough dough.

404.changes: Nothing further to change. Your 10/22 note already found the brown-sugar overage independently (NYT halved everything but the wine and sugar); the directions already include the option to skip the pan-juice reduction, matching Silver Palate's original.

405.changes: Roast the whole squash (split, both halves) instead of dicing and sauteing the raw neck — a 400-vote commenter with 25 years' experience does this for more caramelization, likely fixing the 'squashy' raw flavor your 1/24 note flagged.

406.changes: Extend the first bake to 22-25 minutes; readers repeatedly found raw dough at the centre at 15 minutes as written. Add 5-10 minutes to the second bake for full crispness.

407.changes: Nothing worth changing. It's already the original hot-water-soda version, not the modern Nestle recipe, and it's Mom's tested standard. The all-butter-vs-shortening spread debate is a taste preference, not an error.

414.changes: Peel the celery before chopping (the one substantive tip, 109 votes) - removes the stringy fibers and improves texture noticeably for almost no extra effort.

415.changes: Nothing worth changing. Your note already confirms it's excellent with basmati, and comments say this is the better of two Franey turmeric-rice versions on the site.

418.changes: Nothing worth changing. The recipe already does what the author herself confirms is correct: raw onions go back in with the seared chicken, and olives keep their pits for flavor.

419.changes: Nothing worth changing. Your Dec 2024 note already confirms excellent results using the metric measures as written; don't overbake past pale gold, per the author's own warning.

424.changes: Nothing worth changing. The built-in instant-read checks (start at 45 min, pull at 120F, rest to 125F) already prevent the main risk commenters flag; the reverse-sear debate is genuinely split, not a confirmed fix.

425.changes: Your 3/23 note found the batter stayed thick even after adding extra buttermilk; start with 2 1/4 cups (545 g) buttermilk instead of 2 cups to prevent it.

432.changes: Your 2/18 note already found the fixes: use 12 oz cheese (50% more) and move to the middle rack - with two convection ovens, bottom-rack burning is likely, not a fluke of the old kitchen.

434.changes: Skip the salt-and-ice-weight drain: the top-voted tip (624 votes) says to scoop out seeds first, smash lightly, then air-dry on a plate instead - faster, less fuss, same crunch.

446.changes: Simmer the pork closer to an hour, not 40-45 minutes, per the Serious Eats tester's own retest; top up with extra orange juice/water if it dries out first.

447.changes: Keep the griddle at medium (~275°F); reader reports say too-hot griddle is the main failure. Use about 2 Tbsp clarified butter, not the full 6 Tbsp — readers found that's plenty. Your 1/16 note's method is otherwise correct.

460.changes: Reserve 2-3 Tbsp of the mayo-sour cream dressing separately and stir it into leftovers instead of premixing it all in; the full batch dries out in the fridge over a few days.

463.changes: Skip the 1/2 tsp salt in the dressing; the 2 Tbsp soy sauce already salts it, and an 84-vote reader found the full amount too salty. Keep salting the cucumbers separately — that step controls texture, not seasoning.

468.changes: Flatten cookies partway through baking, about 10 minutes in, not before — that produces Chang's chewy crumb; pre-flattening raw dough loses the effect. Family copy's 1/4 tsp cinnamon vs. published 1 tsp: split the difference at 1/2 tsp.

469.changes: Nothing worth changing. The method (salt before cooking, gentle heat, water not milk, fold and pull off while wet) is sound and uncontested; commenters raised no technique issues.

471.changes: Raise the bath to 185°F and extend to 90 min for standard chunks; several readers found carrots still firm at 183°F/1hr as printed. Weight the bag so it doesn't float — trapped steam causes uneven cooking.
